headline: India reopens after Tuesday's holiday with GIFT Nifty pointing to a gap-up of roughly 1%, as it catches up with the global rebound it missed. But Asian tech stocks are crashing again this morning, so the early gain may not hold.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: The dashboard's four direction checks add up to +17 out of 100 (neutral), and they disagree two against two, so conviction is low. Market data as of Monday's close; overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: GIFT Nifty was around **25,710–25,773** near 8 am, well above Monday's Nifty close of 25,350, so a higher open looks likely as India catches up after the holiday.
Asian chip stocks are falling hard this morning (Taiwan **−7.4%**, Korea −6%, Japan −3.3%) after Nvidia fell about 6% in the US. This is the main threat to the gap-up.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought ₹5,673 crore of Indian shares on Monday even as Nifty fell 1.75%. Monday's fall came from local selling and profit-taking, not from foreigners leaving.
My call: a bounce at the open is more likely than a fall, but I have low confidence it lasts all day. A slide back below 25,350 would show the bounce failed.
Reports say the US plans new tariffs on 16 countries, with India possibly facing a higher rate than Japan or Europe. Nothing official yet.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: India gets the good news it missed on Tuesday, but this morning's news is worse, so the night works only partly against Monday's fall.

points.text: GIFT Nifty was up about **1.1%** on its own last price at 8 am. Part of its gap over Nifty is the normal futures premium of about 40 points, so the real signal is roughly a 300–400 point higher open.
Indian shares listed in the US rose on Tuesday while India was shut: Infosys **+3.2%**, HDFC Bank +1.6%, ICICI Bank +1.2%, and the India fund (INDA) +1.2%.
Since Tuesday evening, the Nasdaq fell **1.5%** and the S&P 500 fell 0.5%. Nasdaq futures are down another 1.4% this morning, led by chip stocks.
Asia this morning: Taiwan −7.4% and Korea −6% (after a record jump on Tuesday), Japan −3.3%, Shanghai −1.1%. Only Hong Kong is up (+0.6%).
Brent crude is at $90, up 0.6% since Tuesday evening, but down 22% over the past month. Gold fell 2.3%. The US 10-year rate and the dollar barely moved.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: A bounce at the open looks more likely, but with low confidence that it holds through the day.

points.text: For a bounce: Monday's 1.75% fall came while FIIs were buying (a 10-day buying streak in the dashboard data), and Nifty is still above all three of its moving averages.
For a bounce: India missed Tuesday's global rally, and US-listed Indian shares rose 1–3%. GIFT Nifty is already pricing this in.
For a fall: Asian tech shares are being sold hard right now, US futures are lower, and fresh US tariff talk names India.
Fear is rising: India VIX (expected swings) is **17.9**, higher than 81% of the past year. Big moves in both directions are more likely than usual.
What would prove me wrong: if the gap-up fades and Nifty falls back below Monday's close of 25,350, sellers are still in charge, and 25,000 is the next level to watch.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The longer trend is still up, but positioning in futures turned weaker on Monday.

points.text: Price trend (+2 of 2): Nifty at 25,350 is above its 20-day (24,526), 50-day and 200-day averages, with higher highs and higher lows.

Futures (−2 of 2): prices fell while open contracts rose 15%, and FII bets on a rise fell from 34% to **20%** of their index futures. Monday was probably the November contract's last day (moved up for the holiday), which can distort these numbers.
Options (+1.3 of 2): option sellers added protection-selling (put writing) at 24,800–25,000, building a floor there. Traders also bought calls at 25,500–25,900.
Put-call ratio (how many bets on a fall vs bets on a rise) is 0.92, down from 1.03 five days ago. Not stretched either way, so score 0.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreigners keep buying Indian shares in cash, while domestic funds took profits.

points.text: FIIs bought a net **₹5,673 crore** on Monday, almost the size of their 20-day average daily flow (₹6,153 crore). They have bought ₹1.18 lakh crore so far in November.
Domestic funds (DIIs) sold ₹2,760 crore on Monday and ₹64,547 crore this month. Usually it is the other way round, so this is unusual.
NSDL data shows FIIs bought ₹10,915 crore of IT shares and ₹11,065 crore of telecom shares in the second half of October.
In index futures, FIIs now hold about four bets on a fall for every bet on a rise (20% long). That is lower than last week but not in the under-10% zone where a fast reversal usually starts.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Fear about AI stocks and possible US rate hikes is the main global worry, while cheaper oil helps India.

points.text: Nvidia fell about 6% on Tuesday after a 31% jump on Monday, when Jensen Huang returned as CEO. Doubts about returns on AI spending are hitting chip-heavy markets like Taiwan and Korea hardest.
US 6-month Treasury bills pay **4.46%**, well above the Fed rate of 3.88%. This suggests the market expects the Fed to raise rates, which usually pulls money out of countries like India.
US fear gauge (VIX) is at 26.4, higher than 95% of the past year. The S&P 500 is down 6% in a month.
Brent crude is down **22%** in a month, to $90. Cheaper oil lowers India's import bill and inflation.
The rupee is 2.4% stronger against the dollar in a month (₹92.91), which makes Indian shares more attractive to foreigners.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No Nifty 50 company reported this week, so results won't move the index today.

points.text: 11 small companies filed results in the last 7 days. None are in the Nifty 50.
The calendar shows no Nifty 50 results due in the next two weeks.
Infosys's US listing rose 3.2% on Tuesday, so IT stocks may start the day firm. The selloff in Asia is in chipmakers, which India has very few of.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: US inflation data tonight, India's GDP on Monday and the RBI on 4 December are the big events.

points.text: Tonight 7 pm IST: US core PCE inflation (forecast 0.3%) and US GDP. A hot inflation number would add to fears of a Fed rate hike.
Mon 30 Nov, 4 pm: India's quarterly GDP. A big surprise either way can move the whole market.
Fri 4 Dec, 10 am: RBI rate decision. Then the US Fed decides on 10 Dec (around midnight IST).
Any official US tariff announcement naming India at a higher rate would hurt exporters and could stall the India-US trade deal.

levels.note: A close above 25,500 would mean call sellers there gave way and the uptrend is back on; a close below 25,000 would break the put floor and point to a deeper fall.

watch.text: How much of the GIFT Nifty gap-up shows up at the open, and whether it holds in the first hour.
Bank stocks: they led Monday's fall (Bank Nifty −3%). HDFC Bank and ICICI rose in the US on Tuesday.
Taiwan and Korea through the day. A deeper slide there could drag the rest of Asia, India included.
US core PCE inflation and GDP. A hot number would raise Fed hike fears.
Evening FII/DII data: does the FII buying streak continue?

bottom_line: India should open higher as it catches up with the global rebound it missed on Tuesday, and foreigners are still buying. But Asian tech stocks are crashing this morning, US futures are lower, and US tariff news names India, so the gap-up may fade. The dashboard is neutral (+17) with its checks split two against two, so confidence is low. The main risk is the AI-stock selloff spreading, and a slip back below 25,350 would mean the bounce failed.
